title: ValueLog: social value tracking and reports for small public-sector suppliers
summary: UK public contracts now weigh "social value" (local jobs, apprentices, volunteering, carbon) and ask suppliers to report against promised KPIs. Small facility, cleaning and construction suppliers track this in spreadsheets. ValueLog collects the evidence from staff and records, and produces the quarterly report each council wants.
hook: "We promised the council 2 apprentices and 200 volunteering hours. Now they want quarterly evidence in their portal and I have no idea where it is."
story:
**David runs a cleaning and facilities company with 60 staff** that holds contracts with two councils and an NHS trust. To win them, his bid writer promised social value: **local hires, an apprentice, school visits and volunteering hours**, plus carbon reduction. Each buyer now asks for quarterly evidence, but in **different formats and portals**.

His office manager spends two days each quarter chasing supervisors for photos, timesheets and names, then filling in three different templates. If the numbers are low, the KPI may be published under the new procurement rules, and it could hurt the next bid. He needs one place where staff log activities as they happen and reports come out ready.
whyNow: The Procurement Act 2023 went live in February 2025, with more transparency on contract KPIs. In 2026 the government consulted on further reforms that put more weight on skills and jobs. SMEs say social value is an admin burden, and the number of buyer reporting platforms keeps growing.
evidence: 76% of respondents to techUK's 2023 SME survey said addressing social value is an administrative burden [techUK]
Under the Procurement Act, social value KPIs can be published, exposing shortfalls; some organisations hold back from publishing while they test what they can deliver [Social Value Portal]
Local authorities and suppliers say a growing number of reporting platforms makes consistent social value data harder [Socitm]
Social Value Portal does not publish supplier pricing; its Social Value Academy training costs £375 one-off [G2 / FitGap]
A buyer-side platform on G-Cloud charges public buyers £8,000 a year for up to 75 contracts, with free supplier access [GOV.UK Digital Marketplace]

whyReal.title: It decides contracts
whyReal.text: Social value is a scored part of public tenders, and promises made in the bid must be delivered and reported.

whyReal.title: Reporting is fragmented
whyReal.text: Each council or trust may use a different portal or template. Suppliers with several contracts report the same work several times.

whyReal.title: Platforms are built for buyers
whyReal.text: Most social value platforms are bought by councils to measure suppliers. Few help the small supplier collect its own evidence.

whyReal.title: Jonatan knows these suppliers
whyReal.text: Facility, cleaning and construction services are big public-sector suppliers and exactly Jonatan's field.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: UK SMEs (10–250 staff) holding public contracts: facility services, cleaning, security, construction, maintenance, catering, IT services.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: managing director, bid manager or office manager.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK; later Ireland and EU countries where green and social criteria in public procurement are growing.

solution.title: Load the promises
solution.text: upload the bid answers and contract KPIs; AI turns them into a list of measurable targets per contract.

solution.title: Log as it happens
solution.text: supervisors log activities from their phone (apprentice started, school visit, volunteering hours) with photos and names.

solution.title: Pull in data
solution.text: import payroll postcodes for local-hire rates, training records and fuel/energy data for carbon.

solution.title: Track progress
solution.text: a dashboard shows each KPI against target, with warnings before the quarter ends.

solution.title: Report in their format
solution.text: export each buyer's template or TOMs-style report, plus case studies written by AI from logged activities, ready for the next bid.

must: Contracts and KPI targets (AI from bid text)
CSV import for staff postcodes and training
later: Templates for the most common buyer portals
Bid library: reuse evidence in new tenders

techStack: LLM for KPI extraction and case studies

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Jonatan interviews 15 facility and construction suppliers with public contracts; collect 5 real reporting templates.
Dashboard, imports, report export and case-study writer.
3 suppliers produce a real quarterly report in ValueLog.

risks.answer: Export in each portal's format; the value is collecting evidence once.
UK has thousands of SME public suppliers; EU green procurement is a later market.
Sell before quarter-end and during bids; show the bid-library benefit.
Keep KPI types flexible; AI maps any bid text to targets.

questions: How many public contracts with social value KPIs do you hold?
How do you collect the evidence each quarter, and how long does it take?
How many different reporting formats or portals do you use?
Has missing evidence ever hurt a contract review or a new bid?
Would £49–119 a month for one place to log and report be worth it?
